title: Machine-learning screening finds previously unreported antibacterial compounds active against Burkholderia and ESKAPE pathogens
summary: A directed-message-passing neural network trained on a 29,537-compound Burkholderia cenocepacia screen prioritized compounds from a natural-product library. Laboratory testing found five previously uncharacterized compounds that inhibited B. cenocepacia; 22 of 43 tested prioritized compounds inhibited at least one of five ESKAPE pathogens.
ai_technology: Directed-message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) implemented with Chemprop

evidence.tested: Laboratory testing found five previously uncharacterized compounds that inhibited B. cenocepacia; 22 of 43 tested prioritized compounds inhibited at least one of five ESKAPE pathogens.
evidence.unknown: The compounds were active in vitro; no clinical effect, safety or therapeutic readiness is established. Several confirmed compounds were known antimicrobials, while five natural-product hits were described as previously uncharacterized. An inferred RpoB mechanism for STL558147 was suggested by CRISPRi sensitivity rather than directly demonstrated binding.
evidence.ai_role: The D-MPNN ranked FDA-approved and natural-product library molecules for predicted antibacterial activity; researchers tested high-ranked compounds in bacterial growth assays and confirmed activity. It was a screening-prioritization tool, not evidence of clinical efficacy.
